label: prf:q-beta-radius-of-convergence-gate
title: Proof of q beta radius of convergence gate
html:
Proof

Write c_k for the pinned ladder coefficients at the substrate anchor (canonical SDP extraction, qbeta-decay-sdp-extended-ck.witness.json), g(u) := \sum_{k \ge 2} c_k u^k for the log-correction generating function, and u_0 := u_{\text{substrate}} \approx 0.00852.

Step 1 — rationality of g. By the c_k recursion, the ladder coefficients of any admissible candidate Habiro element F(q) satisfy a depth-d linear recursion with constant (q_0-rational) coefficients, c_{k+1} = \sum_{j=1}^{d} a_j\,c_{k+1-j}. A sequence satisfying such a recursion has a rational generating function: multiplying the recursion by u^{k+1} and summing gives g(u) = P(u)/Q(u) with Q(u) = 1 - \sum_{j=1}^{d} a_j u^j and \deg P \le d + 1. The singularities of g are therefore exclusively poles, located at the reciprocals 1/r of the roots r of the characteristic polynomial \chi(x) = x^d - \sum_{j=1}^{d} a_j x^{d-j} (with multiplicities, up to cancellation against P). No branch points and no essential singularities can occur, and the radius of convergence of the series is 1/|r_{\max}| for r_{\max} a characteristic root of maximal modulus surviving cancellation.

Step 2 — asymptotic signature of a simple dominant pole. Suppose the dominant root r_{\max} is unique (no other root of equal modulus) with multiplicity \mu, and set \rho := 1/r_{\max}. Partial fractions give c_k = C\,k^{\mu-1} r_{\max}^{\,k}\,\bigl(1 + o(1)\bigr) for some constant C \ne 0. Two consequences:

  1. Ratio test. c_{k+1}/c_k \to r_{\max} = 1/\rho.
  2. Normalized magnitude. c_k\,\rho^k = C\,k^{\mu-1}(1 + o(1)): a flat (constant) asymptote is the exact signature of \mu = 1, a simple pole. For \mu \ge 2 the sequence must grow by the factor ((k+1)/k)^{\mu-1}, at least 12.5\,\% per step at k = 8; a dominant complex-conjugate pair would instead make c_k \rho^k oscillate with the argument of r_{\max}.

Within the rational class forced by Step 1, these finite-order signatures are therefore decisive: flatness of c_k \rho^k together with convergence of the ratio identifies a unique simple dominant pole at u = \rho.

Step 3 — locating the canonical pole. The pinned c_2, \ldots, c_{10} exhibit exactly the simple-pole signature at \rho = u_0 (table below): the ratio c_{k+1}/c_k converges to 1/u_0 \approx 117.4 by k = 10; the normalized magnitudes c_k\,u_0^k for k \in \{8, 9, 10\} agree at \approx 2.118 \times 10^{-13} with 0.02\,\% spread — flat to 2 \times 10^{-4} per step, excluding \mu \ge 2 (which forces \ge 12\,\% growth) and a dominant complex pair (which forces oscillation); and the log-slope fit of \ln(c_k u_0^k) against \ln k gives exponent \beta \approx 0.999 against the calibration c_k \rho^k \sim k^{\beta-1}, forcing the integer \mu = \beta = 1. Hence the canonical generating function has a unique dominant simple pole at u = u_0, within the resolution of the k \le 10 window. The location is anchor-stable: re-pinning from the proton to the muon anchor shifts u_0 by only 2.10 \times 10^{-7} relative (210 ppb, table below).

Step 4 — gate direction and tolerance. Let F be a candidate generating coefficients \tilde c_k by the same recursion mechanism, with rational \tilde g(u) = \sum_k \tilde c_k u^k (Step 1 applies verbatim) and nearest pole \tilde u_0. Suppose |\tilde u_0 - u_0|/u_0 > 10^{-6}. If \tilde c_k = c_k for all sufficiently large k, then \tilde g - g would be a polynomial, so \tilde g and g would have identical poles — contradicting \tilde u_0 \ne u_0. Hence \tilde c_k \ne c_k for arbitrarily large k: the candidate does not generate the canonical ladder, and is refuted at the fibre level, before any canonical-anchor sweep at q_0. The 10^{-6} tolerance is calibrated from below by the cross-anchor swing: the true kernel's pole location moves by only 2.10 \times 10^{-7} under the proton–muon re-pin, so the true kernel always passes (no false refutation), while the tolerance remains nearly 5\times above that swing so that anchor choice can never trip the gate. From above, it is far sharper than the few-percent near-match band delegated to the \S 4(d) direction-sanity gate — the two gates are complementary by construction. \blacksquare
